key_insight: Composition-weighted elemental properties offer a low-cost route to estimating shear-modulus–Burgers-vector products (μbₚ) and screening unstable planar fault energies in multicomponent alloys.
engineering_relevance: This approach could accelerate alloy screening for slip and twinning behavior while reducing reliance on expensive atomistic calculations.
method: Use embedded-atom method (EAM) potentials complemented by density functional theory (DFT).
Evaluate temperature and composition effects on unstable planar fault energies and their relationship to μbₚ.
Estimate multicomponent-alloy μbₚ from composition-weighted pure-element values.
evidence_signal: In the Co–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ni system, alloy μbₚ correlates linearly with composition-weighted elemental μbₚ (R² = 0.95), while the fault-energy correlation strengthens with chemical complexity.
watch_item: Elemental averaging systematically overestimates alloy μbₚ, and fault-energy scaling deviates for intermetallics, non-close-packed elements, and some binary compositions.
paper_title: Predicting unstable planar fault energies in multicomponent alloys from pure elemental components
